method.harm: max(original-H mean deficit of policy minus paired Static mean deficit, 0)
method.family_contribution: sum(case tail weight * case harm within family) / global 0.10*N case mass
method.cutoff_ties: Exact stored-value ties at the global cutoff share the remaining tail mass equally. Near-equal values are not merged. This preserves global CVaR and avoids family-order-dependent attribution.
method.zero_cutoff: Zero-harm cases may share remaining mass when fewer than 10% of cases have positive harm; their contribution is zero.
method.zero_cvar: Contribution percentages are null when global CVaR is zero; absolute contributions remain defined.
method.scope_of_denominator: All family contributions share one regime-wide cutoff and global tail denominator.
method.largest_case_order: descending positive hybrid harm; exact ties broken by declared family order then seed
method.largest_case_limit: Five cases are shown even if some harms are zero; zero harm is not classified as an adverse event.

metric_windows.dropped: cumulative dropped work at original H
metric_windows.tail_dropped: additional dropped work in the fixed 32-minute follow-up
metric_windows.total_dropped: all dropped work over original H plus 32-minute follow-up
metric_windows.tail_auc_deficit: sum of deficit over the fixed 32-minute follow-up

limitations: Descriptive attribution after outcomes; no simulation, policy selection, acceptance change or tuning.
Family contribution reflects both case frequency and harm magnitude under the original equal-case weighting.
Tail families and largest cases identify observed residual harm, not a proven causal mechanism.
Development cases are known data. Repeated analyses or simulations do not add independent cases.
Any proposed policy change requires a new study and untouched validation data.
